extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants, patent practitioners/attorneys, and USPTO patent examiners handling Information Disclosure Statements (IDS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing, filing, and examiner handling of Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98, including timing, the required statement under 1.97(e), fees, content/format, cure opportunities, and consequences of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirements for IDS (37 CFR 1.97)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an IDS will be considered by the Office depends on when it is filed relative to prosecution events (e.g., before/after mailing of Office actions, after prosecution closes, before/after payment of issue fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information is submitted during the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with a statement under 37 CFR 1.97(e) and used in a new ground of rejection on unamended claims, the next Office action will not be made final (applicant submitted information promptly and prior to a final determination). If a new ground of rejection was necessitated by amendment by applicant, the IDS submitted with a fee under 37 CFR 1.17(p) may be used and the next Office action can be made final (see MPEP §706.07(a)). An IDS filed on or after the mailing date of a final action, notice of allowance, or other action that closes prosecution but before or simultaneous with payment of the issue fee will be considered only if accompanied by a statement under 37 CFR 1.97(e) and the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(p) (this is treated as a late-stage submission). IDS filed after the issue fee has been paid generally will not be considered and will be placed in the application file (see MPEP §609.05(b)), though limited programs (e.g., QPIDS) or petitions under 37 CFR 1.313 may permit consideration in narrow circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement required under 37 CFR 1.97(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS accompanied by a 37 CFR 1.97(e) statement must state either (1) each item was first cited in a communication from a foreign patent office in a counterpart foreign application not more than three months prior to filing the statement, or (2) that no item was cited in such a communication and, to the signer’s knowledge after making reasonable inquiry, no item was known to any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) more than three months prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two alternative statements may be used; exact statutory language is encouraged but not required if the meaning is identical. The three-month period is measured from the communication mailing date by the foreign office; receipt dates by counsel/associates do not begin the period. A counterpart foreign application excludes a PCT international application designating the U.S. for purposes of 1.97(e) (applicants must consider applicability of 1.97(e)(2) in international applications). A single IDS may include two lists and two statements (or designate which statement applies to which citations); only one fee is required if both statements/lists are submitted the same day. A statement under 1.97(e) need not be an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.68 and will be accepted as dispositive of compliance absent evidence to the contrary. Sample wording is provided in the MPEP. Certain items (e.g., where an inventor is also a named author of a cited item) cannot be covered by 1.97(e)(2) for that item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement for late IDS (37 CFR 1.17(p))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed after prosecution has closed but before payment of the issue fee must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p) for the IDS to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of the fee and submission of a proper 37 CFR 1.97(e) statement are essential for consideration at this late prosecution stage, assuming content requirements of 37 CFR 1.98 are satisfied. If the fee or statement is missing, the IDS will be placed in the file but not considered. See form paragraphs (e.g., 13.09) for examiner notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form requirements for IDS (37 CFR 1.98)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS must meet the content and format requirements of 37 CFR 1.98: the list must be submitted as a separate paper (not incorporated into the specification), include all patents/publications/applications being submitted, list U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications separately from other documents, include the application number on each page, provide a blank column for examiner initials, and have a heading clearly indicating it is an information disclosure statement; legible copies of cited foreign patent documents and non-patent literature are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with any of these content/format requirements leads to non-consideration of the IDS (placed in the file but not considered). Examples/form paragraphs for specific defects are provided (¶6.49 series): references listed in the specification (¶6.49.06), missing copies of references (¶6.49.07), non-compliant list format (¶6.49.08), etc. If only some items fail to comply, the examiner should draw a line through non-complying citations and consider those that do comply. Use of PTO/SB/08 or its equivalent is expected; the examiner will initial considered citations on the list. If an IDS is resubmitted or corrected, the date of the resubmission is the operative date for timing compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise explanation for non-English language information (37 CFR 1.98(a)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each non-English reference cited in an IDS, a concise explanation of relevance (as presently understood by the individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) most knowledgeable about the content) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the foreign search report is not required to satisfy this requirement, but an English-language version may be submitted to help satisfy the concise explanation. Examiners will consider non-English information in view of the concise explanation and what is understandable on its face (e.g., drawings, chemical formulas) and need not require a translation. However, the examiner’s presumption of consideration is limited to the portion translated/concisely explained (see Semiconductor Energy Laboratory Co. v. Samsung Electronics Co.). Applicants are encouraged to provide English-language material where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic medium and filing method requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: IDS submissions must be made on acceptable electronic media or via the USPTO patent electronic filing system (EFS) in compliance with USPTO electronic filing requirements; some media (e.g., read-only optical discs submitted outside EFS) may be non-acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an IDS is submitted on an electronic medium that is not acceptable, it will be placed in the application file but the information will not be considered (¶6.49.10). Certain large items (Large Tables, Sequence Listings, computer-readable sequence listings, Computer Program Listing Appendices) may be submitted on read-only optical discs as allowed by 37 CFR 1.52(e), but most IDS documents should be submitted via EFS. Forms PTOL-90/PTO-90C referenced for after-issue-fee submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner marking and acknowledgement of IDS consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must indicate which citations in an IDS have been considered and which have not (traditionally by initials adjacent to considered citations and strike-through of non-considered citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where compliant, the examiner will initial considered citations on PTO/SB/08 (or use the alternative electronic signature method stamping each page with 'All references considered except where lined through' with electronic initials). The examiner must also fill in the examiner’s name and the date the information was considered on the form. A copy of the reviewed PTO/SB/08 will be returned to applicant with the next communication to acknowledge receipt and indicate which references were considered. The original listing will be entered into the file. Examiners should draw a line through citations not considered. For non-English references, consideration is indicated in the same manner as English references but the presumption is limited to what is explained/translated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of non-compliance and correction/resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Information submitted that fails to comply with timing, fee, statement, or content requirements (37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98) will be placed in the application file but will not be considered by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants will be informed of noncompliance using form paragraphs (6.49 through 6.49.10) specifying the reason (e.g., missing statement, missing fee, improper list format, missing copies, non-English explanation missing, unacceptable medium). The applicant may file a new IDS or correct the defect, but the date of the new IDS/correction is the operative date for timing/compliance purposes. If only some items are non-compliant, the examiner will strike through only those items and consider the remainder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide attempt and time to cure inadvertent omissions (37 CFR 1.97(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: No extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b) are permitted for filing an IDS, but if a bona fide attempt was made to comply with content requirements and part of the required content is inadvertently omitted, the Office may allow additional time to complete compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a bona fide attempt is evident, applicant is given ONE (1) MONTH from the notice date to supply omissions or corrections (form paragraph 6.51). No extensions of that one-month period may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136. This cure opportunity does not apply where there has been a deliberate omission or when timing requirements themselves were not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quick Path IDS (QPIDS) pilot and petitions under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw from issue
rubrics_metrics.description: IDS filed after the issue fee has been paid are generally not considered, but the QPIDS pilot (launched May 2012) and certain petitions under 37 CFR 1.313 may permit consideration prior to grant under specific circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information about the QPIDS Pilot is available on the USPTO website; QPIDS allows, in narrow circumstances, submission of IDS after issue fee payment but before patent grant. Alternatively, petitioner may file petitions under 37 CFR 1.313(c)(2) or (c)(3) to withdraw the application from issue so the IDS may be considered with a concurrent RCE, CPA, or continuing application. Applicants are encouraged to file such petitions and accompanying RCE/CPA/continuing application via EFS or facsimile; if filing a petition by facsimile because IDS size makes facsimile impracticable, the petition need not be accompanied by the IDS but should indicate the IDS will be filed in the continuing application. The Office cannot ensure petitions will be acted upon prior to the patent grant, so applicants should contact the Office of Petitions to confirm timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IDS materials submitted as part of applicant’s reply to an Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents submitted by applicant in reply to an Office action (e.g., affidavits, declarations, patents, printed publications) may be relied on by the applicant to show operability or meaning and may be considered as part of applicant’s reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such documents may be in any form; when submitted and relied upon by applicant in a reply, the examiner should treat and consider them accordingly as part of the prosecution record. If submitted as part of a reply, ensure they meet IDS content/format requirements if intended to be an IDS for separate consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable inquiry standard for making 37 CFR 1.97(e)(2) statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A person signing a 1.97(e)(2) statement must have made reasonable inquiry into when the information became known; the statement can be based on present, good faith knowledge without a file search but cannot be made on mere information and belief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registered practitioner representing a foreign client may rely on statements from the foreign client regarding the date the information first became known, but if the practitioner receives information without being informed whether it was known more than three months earlier, the practitioner must make reasonable inquiry before signing 1.97(e)(2). If an inventor gave a publication to prosecuting counsel with intent it be cited, counsel should inquire as to when the inventor became aware of the publication before making 1.97(e)(2). The phrase 'after making reasonable inquiry' requires affirmative inquiry in uncertain situations. A statement made in good faith by a registered practitioner or other individual that the statement was filed within the three-month period will be accepted as dispositive absent evidence to the contrary; challenges to adequacy should be directed to the Office of Patent Legal Administration.
